steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: A Bill must pass through both Houses of Parliament and receive Royal Assent to become an Act

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The legislative process starts with a Green Paper (consultation) then a White Paper (firm proposals)

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: A Bill goes through First Reading, Second Reading, Committee Stage, Report Stage and Third Reading in each House

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The House of Lords can amend and delay Bills but cannot block those passed by the Commons (Parliament Acts)

steps.title: Try it yourself

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Know the full legislative process with all stages in both Houses The Law Commission and pressure groups are common exam topics Explain WHY each stage of the process matters — don't just list them Delegated legislation advantages and disadvantages are frequently tested Use real examples of law reform — e.g. the Domestic Abuse Act 2021 or changes following public campaigns
